title.narrative: Recon: Social entrepeneurship for sustainable development and peace building
Recon: Social entrepeneurship for sustainable development and peace building

description.narrative:
Fundacion RECON (RECON) is a is Colombian NGO that works with vulnerable communities in Colombia searching, supporting and strengthening social entrepreneurships that may generate sustainable economic alternatives to poor populations affected by conflict. The general objective of this contribution is directed to consolidate RECON as the leading organization of social entrepreneurship in Colombia, with the purpose of identifying, inspiring, connecting and strengthening entrepreneurship initiatives and social innovation projects that generate economic and social transformations and environmental sustainability, in vulnerable communities.
This general objective is expected to be achieved by three specific objectives:
1. To consolidate the technical and institutional capacity of RECON, to benefit and facilitate the participation of civil society in construction processes of peace and territorial development through social entrepreneurship initiatives.
2. To promote actions that contribute to strengthening the identification processes and promotion of entrepreneurship and social innovation projects aligned with the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).
3. To develop organizational strategies to strengthen projects of social entrepreneurship, in order to contribute to the consolidation of sustainability and territorial impact.
By the end of this intervention (which is initially planned for four years), RECON is expected to be the leading organisation in the country that groups and strengthens small civil society organisations and supports and accompanies social entrepreneurship projects conceived by vulnerable populations affected by conflict (women, ex-combatants, LGTBI, poor, indigenous and afro-Colombians, among others) with the purpose of generating sustainable economic income and thus contributing to peace-building in the targeted territories.

Fundacion RECON har ansökt om finansiering på 7 500 000 SEK hos Sveriges ambassad i Colombia för att genomföra projektet “Project for the consolidation of the system of social entrepreneurship in Colombia as a tool for sustainable development and peace building” i Colombia under perioden 2020-2023.
Insatsen syftar till att konsolidera RECON som den ledande organisationen för socialt entreprenörskap i landet, i syfte att identifiera, inspirera, sammankoppla och stärka entreprenörskap och initiativ för social innovation som genererar ekonomiska och sociala förändringar och miljömässig hållbarhet i utsatta samhällen genom att 1) konsolidera RECON:s tekniska och institutionella kapacitet, 2) främja åtgärder som bidrar till identifiering och främjande av entreprenörskap och 3) utveckla organisatoriska strategier som stärker sociala entreprenörskap som bidrar till konsolidering av hållbarhet och som har territoriell effekt.
Insatsens totala budget är 7 500 000 SEK.

The purpose of the project support to Recon is to identify, inspire, connect, and strengthen entrepreneurships and social innovation initiatives which generate sustainable socio-economic transformations in conflict-affected communities by: 1) Consolidating RECON’s technical and institutional capacities. 2) Encouraging actions that contribute to the identification of entrepreneurships. 3) Developing organisational strategies that strengthen social entrepreneurships that contribute to the consolidation of sustainability and have territorial impact.

Regarding the results achieved, it is important to mention the Colombian context, with high rates of inequality, exacerbated by high inflation and increased living costs. Hence, social entrepreneurship is one important tool for boosting local economic development, particularly targeting vulnerable populations in Colombia.
The public calls
Through the public calls, 792 social entrepreneurships were identified, making the RECON network bigger and now constituting of over 5000 social entrepreneurships, and therefore becoming the biggest bank for social entrepreneurships in the country. Furthermore, the networks now include initiatives from 28 out of the 32 departments. The majority contributes to sustainable development and the environment (312 registered), 236 to poverty and reducing inequalities, 84 to sustainable peace and human rights, 74 to health, 47 to tech for good and 39 to efficient resource management. The calls have proven to be key for identifying and strengthening social entrepreneurship in conflict-affected municipalities, and to provide visibility for RECON and in turn Swedish support. Major improvements to the RECON platform in 2021 led to an increased the visibility of the social entrepreneurs.
The project did not include funds for acceleration. However, RECON developed a fund, that leveraged private financial and technical investments amounting of more than 400.000USD, to improve some identified social entrepreneurs. A programme was created with 15 modules that focused on increasing capacities and offering tools to strengthen the social entrepreneur as an agent for change and consolidate the model of social entrepreneurships. Six social entrepreneurs with a total of 5.200 beneficiaries, and with 85 employees were selected for the incubation process. Through this, their social business model could scale up and grow, and therefore maximize their impact and improve their sustainability. In addition, thanks to the investments received, these supported entrepreneurs created 60% more employment.
The Law
Furthermore, as was one of the follow-up recommendations from the management letter following the mid-term evaluation, RECON has provided inputs and support for promoting the integration of the Social Entrepreneurship Law to the Ministry of Commerce, who oversee implementing the law. RECONs support was a key element in both providing inputs to the Congress for the debates, as well as with the Presidency to impulse the sanction of the law. The Law is the first in Latin America that recognizes social entrepreneurship, and that in theory ensures that the national government creates a public policy for social entrepreneurship and develops strategies to strengthen social entrepreneurs in vulnerable communities, guaranteeing inclusion of a territorial and differential approach. It also promotes and provides social entrepreneurs with new strategies for their financial stability, such as training by the state and access to credit. While the law is in place, RECON emphasizes that there has been a lack of political will to implement the law, referring to delays in necessary definitions, budget allocation and coordination between the governmental entities and the civil society. Inclusion of objectives in the National Development Plan
During 2023, in part thanks to the advocacy carried out by RECON, objectives on social entrepreneurship were included in the National Development Plans. This represents a major achievement of the work of RECON with public policy incidence. However, it remains to be seen to what extent these are included in the local development plans.
Report
During 2023, the third version of the report on Social Entrepreneurship in Colombia Radiografía de Emprendimiento Social en Colombia was launched. This provides a mapping report of the social entrepreneurship in Colombia, including opportunities and difficulties, and includes more than 1000 social entrepreneurs. Many of the arguments later in the debates around the law proposal rose from the previous two reports carried out in 2018 and 2020, which demonstrates the usage of the mapping as a tool to motivate public policies for social entrepreneurship. Furthermore, the report indicated that 64.63% of the social entrepreneurs considers that the lack of financial support, governmental support and access to education limits the development of their social entrepreneurships. The information gathered from the social entrepreneurs were later used to fill in these gaps. For example, 65% of those identified as wanting financial support but never had received such support in the report, now were offered improved opportunities for funding and investment.
